blocks.text: These commands inspect and manipulate a running (or stopped) container without rebuilding it; any change they make lives only in that container.

rows: New process in the running container's namespaces and cgroup
Gets configured env, not vars exported by the entrypoint; running containers only
PID 1's stdout/stderr via the logging driver
Empty if the app logs to files; works on exited containers
Works on stopped containers; changes vanish on recreate
No tools needed in the image
Live CPU, memory, net, block I/O from cgroups

blocks.text:
$ docker exec -it api bash
$ docker exec -u root api apt list --installed
$ docker logs -f --tail 100 --since 10m -t api
$ docker cp api:/app/debug.json ./
No shell to exec into. Borrow tools from a debug container that shares namespaces:
Fixes applied with exec or cp live only in that container's writable layer and disappear on recreate. Put them in the Dockerfile or Compose file.

Q: "How do you debug a container with no shell?" A: "Run a debug image such as netshoot that joins its PID and network namespaces with --pid container:<name> --network container:<name>, or use docker debug where available, and read docker logs and inspect from outside."
